Date : 10/06/2024 ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL) The present petition has been filed seeking a direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondent authorities to award statutory interest over the awarded amount as per Section 80 of the Right To Fair Compensation And Transparency In Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
Thakor Amaratbhai Maganbhai vs State Of Gujarat on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110082027/
1 2013 ["Act of 2013"
for short] effectively from the date of the possession of the land in question till the date of its realization.

sentences.text: 2. It is argued by the learned counsel for the petitioners that statutory interest of 9% & 15% from the date of taking possession NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/8282/2024 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2024 undefined until the awarded amount is paid or deposited, is necessarily to be included in the land acquisition award which has been prepared under Section 23 of the Act of 2013.
The contention is that this element of interest for deprivation of the right of the petitioners to enjoy the land till the awarded amount is deposited, cannot be denied by the award making authority.

3. On the said submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners when we have gone through the award dated 30.07.2021, it is evident that apart from all other elements of compensation, an amount at the rate of 9% from the date of taking possession has been awarded.

The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that 9% over the compensation amount which is indicated in the award is computed as rent of the land in question and it is not the interest on the compensation amount within the meaning of Section 80 of the Act of 2013.
A perusal of the award indicates that an amount of Rs.18,25,939/- was paid to the land owners at the time of taking possession, after issuance of Notification under Sections 11(1) of the Act of 2013.
The award indicates that Notification under Section 11(1) of the Act of 2013 was published on 20.04.2019.

The date of taking possession of the land in question, however, has not been disclosed in the award nor any determination of interest at the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/8282/2024 ORDER DATED:
10/06/2024 undefined rate of 9% from the date of taking possession and at the rate of 15% after one year from the date of taking possession has been computed under the award.

It is evident that the petitioners have been forcibly dispossessed of the land in property after issuance of Notification under Section 11(1) on payment of advance compensation without declaration of the award.
The award though has been declared only on 30.07.2021, but as against the mandate of the Act of, 2013.
Insofar as amended award is concerned, the same pertains to implementation of Factor-2, as determined by the State Government with regard to the land pertaining to the rural area.

3.1. A perusal of the award indicates that though all other elements of compensation under the Act of 2013 have been included in the award but while determining the statutory interest under Section 80 of the Act of 2013, 9% interest has been computed from the date of taking possession of the land in question till the date of issuance of acquisition notifications under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
4.

It is submitted by the learned Assistant Government Pleader appearing for the State respondents that, in those cases, where the possession is given by the land owners, for the period of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/8282/2024 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2024 undefined dispossession i.e. until the date of issuance of the acquisition notification, the rent of the land in question is being paid to the tenure holders at the rate of 9% of the market value.

The submission is that there is, thus, no requirement of payment of interest under Section 80 of the Act of 2013 as rent for the period of dispossession at the rate of 9% of the current market value has already been determined.

2 5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking note of the above submissions, we find that in this case the petitioners have been deprived of their landed property, their right to enjoy the land, and the determination of compensation under the award dated 30.07.2021 has been made after an inordinate delay.

The State respondents cannot get away by saying that they would pay 9% of the current market value as rent as applicable in those cases where the tenure holders parted away their lands under agreement.

6. For the forcible dispossession of the petitioners and dereliction on the part of the State respondents in payment of compensation, they are liable to pay statutory interest as payable under Section 80 of the Act of 2013, i.e. at the rate of 9% for the period of 1 year from the date of taking possession and at the rate of 15% after a period of 1 year from the date of taking possession till the date of payment or NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/8282/2024 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2024 undefined deposit of compensation.

7. As the dispute is legal in nature, we dispose of the instant writ petition at the admission stage itself without calling for the counter affidavit, issuing direction to the concerned respondent authorities to modify the award dated 30.07.2021 as per the observations made herein-above.

Fresh computation of statutory interest under Section 80 of the Act of 2013 is to be made by the concerned respondent authorities and the amount determined under the award as rent at the rate of 9% shall be adjusted towards the fresh computation to be made under this order.
The payment, if due, shall be made to the petitioners under the award in question after adjustment of payment already made under the earlier computation.

8. We find substance in the further submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners that 9%
and 15% statutory interest provided under Section 80 of the Act of 2013, is to be computed on the total amount of compensation which includes the market value, solatium as well as additional interest, all elements of compensation as per the decision of the Apex Court in case of Sunder v.
Union of India reported in 2001 (7) SCC 211.
9.

Sunder v.
Union of India reported in 2001 (7) SCC 211

sentences.text: The re-computation of the benefits as per the direction given NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/8282/2024 ORDER DATED: 10/06/2024 undefined above shall be made by the concerned respondent authorities within a period of one (1) month accordingly, and payment be made to the petitioners within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of submission of the copy of this order before the concerned respondent authorities.
10. With the above observation, the writ petition stands disposed of.
